target_customer: Small and medium Brazilian farmers who borrow through independent agro loan advisors; the advisors use the software
problem: Small and mid-sized Brazilian farmers struggle to get timely credit that covers their full need and often fall back on costly overdraft or personal loans.
business_model: Lender plus vertical software for independent loan advisors, funded partly through its own Fiagro credit fund

founders.name: Lucas Martins
founders.background_notes: AgFeed May 2024 says he ran a family farm for six years, worked four years at Goldman Sachs and was a partner at Stone.

founders.name: Jorge Silveira
founders.background_notes: Software engineer for about 20 years per YC page; grandson of coffee growers.

founders.name: Anísio Carossini
founders.background_notes: AgFeed describes his whole career at Banco do Brasil. A search summary of AgFeed also calls him a founding partner; the YC page does not list him.

competitors.name: Traive
competitors.what: Platform helping Brazilian farmers access capital from lenders
competitors.funding_then: pre-Series A of about $2.5M led by SP Ventures, described as a 2020 round

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit origination, scoring and servicing software for a regulated lending niche, built by a team of four including a 20 year engineer.

defensibility.rationale: A network of about 100 accredited independent advisors and its own credit fund give some lock in, but rural credit models can be copied by funded lenders.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Banks and agfintechs such as Agrolend (founded December 2020 per AgFundernews, later raised several rounds) chased the same farmers; no source shows an incumbent buying Verde.

market_need_then: Brazilian farm credit demand was large and small farmers were underserved by banks; agfintech lending was growing in Latin America.

branding.domain_note: Uses verde.agr.br, an agr.br domain rather than a .com.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, logo or voice was found; coverage is about the credit business only.

outcome_analysis: Verde appears to have kept operating after Y Combinator. AgFeed in May 2024 reported about R$40 million raised across equity and its Fiagro, over R$70 million in credit granted to roughly 300 producers, and a plan to double the fund, even though the YC directory marks it Inactive. No shutdown or acquisition source was found, so the Inactive flag is unexplained and the cause is not public.
notes: YC lists Inactive but 2024 press shows an operating business, so exit is left unknown. Seed date is not stated (a few months before May 2024); the $2.7M figure rests on AgFeed, aggregators repeat it. The Fiagro fund of R$25M is a credit fund, not an equity round. Only Traive has a dated source; Agrolend is mentioned in takeover risk but its article date was not confirmed. verde.agr.br could not be fetched (domain not resolvable from this session). No source on name origin or logo.
